title: SIGILL in the child after `fork()` from a non-main thread, inside `threading._after_fork`
one_line_repro: see repro.py -- concurrent multiprocessing.popen_fork.Popen() from worker threads
reliability: 12/12 on the original script, 3/12 on the 109-line reduction (a race)
prior_art: Unreported. The only SIGILL of the whole campaign, across six fleets.
notes: `_launch` line 62 is its `os.fork()`. PyPy runs the after-fork hooks in the CHILD, so `threading._after_fork()` executes there and dies walking a weakref set. The whole stack is ordinary Python; an illegal instruction underneath it means either an RPython `ll_assert` compiled to a trap or JIT-emitted code running in a state that no longer holds -- and forking away from a multi-threaded, JIT-warm process is exactly such a state. The trigger includes re-running `__init__` on an ALREADY-CONSTRUCTED Popen: the parent side of `_launch` succeeds even when the argument is not a Process, because the child raises in `process_obj._bootstrap` and `os._exit()`s, which the parent never sees. Three hand-written minimal attempts all failed to reproduce it, including one that does exactly what the reduction does -- see the report.
